+HOW YOUR ANSWER IS GRADED — each cell you leave in answer_position is compared, one at a time,
+to a frozen expected file. Match the expected cell EXACTLY:
+  - Match the VALUE and its TYPE. A number is compared rounded to 2 decimals, and a bare numeric
+    string ("511.7") equals the number 511.7 — BUT a string the grader cannot parse as a plain
+    number is NOT equal to a number, so never put a thousands separator or currency/percent symbol
+    inside a numeric cell ("11,604.67" and "$12" fail against 11604.67 and 12). Write dates and
+    times as real datetime/time values (carry over the source cell's number_format), not as text.
+    Reproduce text answers verbatim — do not re-case (`.title()`/`.upper()`) or reword the source.
+  - Formulas are recalculated before grading, so a correct standard formula passes. BUT
+    dynamic-array / newer functions (FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE, spilling XLOOKUP) may fail to
+    evaluate in the grader — for those, compute the result in Python and write the literal value.
+    If a formula you write reads cells that are THEMSELVES formulas, open the workbook with
+    `data_only=True` to get their cached results before you compute.
+  - Do EXACTLY what is asked — no embellishment. Do not add IFERROR, extra rounding, reformatting,
+    or a value substitution (e.g. turning a computed 0 into "-") that was not requested, and do not
+    fill cells the requested layout leaves blank — every unrequested change lands on a cell the
+    grader checks and fails the task. Leave error/blank results (e.g. #N/A) as the plain operation
+    produces them. When told to fix or extend an existing formula, keep its exact existing
+    conditions and add ONLY the requested change.
+  - Use the EXACT cells, columns, and thresholds the instruction names (e.g. "C6", "the value in
+    I3", "the blue column" — inspect fills to locate a colored column). If some rows in the answer
+    range already hold worked example formulas/values, replicate that same method for the remaining
+    rows rather than inventing a different one.
+  - answer_position bounds only WHERE you may WRITE. READ and aggregate across the FULL data region
+    (use the sheet's real last row, not the answer range's last row); when rows are deleted the
+    survivors shift up, so rows originally below the answer window can move into it. Before building
+    a lookup, confirm your key is unique in the lookup table — if it is not, key on every
+    distinguishing column.
